# Amazon EMR Serverless

Store Spark and Hive application and job-run metadata without executing code or provisioning compute.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `emrserverless` |
| Signing name | `emr-serverless` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2021-07-13` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records only |
| Selected operations | 14 of 22 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#amazon-emr-serverless) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Nothing runs: SUCCESS is simulated and does not mean Spark or Hive code executed; no scripts or queries are fetched, no workers or networking are provisioned, and no metrics, logs, results or billing are produced.
- Application transitional states are not observable; GetJobRun advances stored job state after returning it, while list and inventory reads do not advance jobs.
- Auto-start starts application metadata when enabled; auto-stop idle timers and execution timeouts are stored but not enforced.
- GetDashboardForJobRun and other dashboard/session APIs are not whitelisted because no honest executable dashboard or session exists.
- Images, worker type specifications, runtime/monitoring/disk-encryption/interactive/scheduler/identity-center/cost-allocation configurations, execution IAM policy, job modes/retries, creation time filters and attempt selection are unsupported and rejected.
- Release labels are checked syntactically rather than against a regional release catalog; capacity is metadata and not allocated; subnet/security group and execution role existence or IAM permissions are not checked.
- No CloudFormation application provider; deletion removes retained job records, and idempotency records remain until state reset.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

## Supported operations

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
[shape whitelist](https://github.com/amjadjibon/tinystack/blob/main/generator/model/profile.json); an enabled operation may reject unsupported options.

| Operation | HTTP binding |
| --- | --- |
| `CancelJobRun` | `DELETE /applications/{applicationId}/jobruns/{jobRunId}` |
| `CreateApplication` | `POST /applications` |
| `DeleteApplication` | `DELETE /applications/{applicationId}` |
| `GetApplication` | `GET /applications/{applicationId}` |
| `GetJobRun` | `GET /applications/{applicationId}/jobruns/{jobRunId}` |
| `ListApplications` | `GET /applications` |
| `ListJobRuns` | `GET /applications/{applicationId}/jobruns` |
| `ListTagsForResource` | `GET /tags/{resourceArn}` |
| `StartApplication` | `POST /applications/{applicationId}/start` |
| `StartJobRun` | `POST /applications/{applicationId}/jobruns` |
| `StopApplication` | `POST /applications/{applicationId}/stop` |
| `TagResource` | `POST /tags/{resourceArn}` |
| `UntagResource` | `DELETE /tags/{resourceArn}` |
| `UpdateApplication` | `PATCH /applications/{applicationId}` |
